entries.title: Direct Evidence
entries.description: A literal phrase or action showing the harm directly.

entries.title: Strong Evidence
entries.description: Clear supporting evidence that strongly indicates the harm.

entries.title: Weak Evidence
entries.description: Limited or indirect evidence that needs corroboration.

entries.title: Insufficient Evidence
entries.description: A mention that is too vague or contextual to prove harm.

entries.title: Dialogue Evidence
entries.description: Quoted speech or direct conversation containing the clue.

entries.title: Scene Evidence
entries.description: Scene description that confirms the event or dynamic.

entries.title: Cross-Sentence Evidence
entries.description: Evidence that only becomes clear across multiple sentences.

entries.title: Relationship Evidence
entries.description: Evidence from family or guardian relationships.

entries.title: Context Evidence
entries.description: Framing that changes how the literal words should be read.

entries.title: Protection Evidence
entries.description: Evidence of safeguarding or rescue instead of harm.
